title: Organization within a Document
text:
Understanding headers and the navigation pane
A heading in writing is a title or subtitle used to introduce and organize sections of text. Headings:
You can readily make headings with a few keystrokes within Google Docs or Microsoft Word. All you need to do is press Ctrl+Alt+(number) on a PC or Cmd+Option+(number) on a Mac to designate a heading level to that particular text.
The navigation pane is an interactive panel automatically generated by headings. If enabled, it appears on the left side of a Google Doc or Word document. It improves:
Read on for details on how to use headings and the navigation pane. Practice the skills described while reading the tutorial, during everyday computing work, and in the practice tasks at the end of this section.

Heading structure
A first order topical heading like “Understanding headers and the navigation pane” above a level 1 heading. A second order heading like “Heading structure” above is a level 2 heading.

title: Organization within a Document
text:
Example heading use cases
These are some examples of how headers can help.

When writing a paper, you can jump from your introduction to your conclusion with a click. This can help you ensure that your introduction and conclusion are argumentatively aligned.
You can tell a collaborator to look at section “XXX” and use the navigation pane to get there.
You can “zoom out” of a long document with headings by looking at the navigation pane. With this view, you can assess questions like “Is everything there that should be?” and “Does this order make sense?”
In Microsoft Word, you can collapse all sections of your document to focus on the one or two that you are currently working on.
